76763.subject: The AI builders want a stop sign
76763.body:
The Atlas

Автор: GenAI Works


Автор: GenAI Works

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/ai-builders-want-stop-sign-genai-works-vupde?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BSJnLhCjJTLq9feZpEQLEXw%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=3MYQGHOvsh5co1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~ms91gbzw~qj-null-null&eid=fz96fz-ms91gbzw-qj
  
Welcome back! Today covers a request from inside four competing labs, a spectrum regulator writing industrial policy, OpenAI seeding the citation graph and a national court system handing AI the case files.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: 1,132 AI insiders asked Washington to hit the brakes: Four chief scientists signed one sentence requesting international pacing tools, in a personal capacity, with no company endorsement. The FCC became an AI infrastructure policy: New import bans on Chinese robots and power inverters run through equipment authorization, and the inverter half lands directly on data center capex. OpenAI is giving 100,000 researchers its best models: The bet sits in a chart nobody is reading, where arXiv math papers crediting ChatGPT grew 7x in five months. The UAE put AI inside its court system: An integrated platform across the full case lifecycle, launching in September, with one function no other judiciary has permitted. PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. 1,132 AI insiders asked Washington to hit the brakes The statement is one sentence: a request that the US government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace automated AI development. The signature list is the business story.  Jakub Pachocki, chief scientist at OpenAI. Jared Kaplan, chief science officer at Anthropic. Shengjia Zhao, chief scientist at Meta AI. Shane Legg, co-founder of Google DeepMind. Dario Amodei.  Ilya Sutskever. John Schulman. Four competing labs, and the people running their research agendas signed the same document. Every signature was made in a personal capacity. No company endorsed it, and that gap carries the commercial content. The reasoning is a plain description of a coordination failure. The labs believe they may be close to automating AI research.  Each company and country faces pressure not to unilaterally slow down. The world lacks the tools to pace the frontier even if everyone wanted to. Coming from the people with the most information, that reads as an admission that self-regulation cannot work here.
